LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 5.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Time Suggested vocabulary morning, afternoon, evening, night, day, late, early, 
Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Time Suggested vocabulary morning, afternoon, evening, night, day, late, early,  in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to look at the person talking to us? 2. Which words do we use to talk about time?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Collaboration: learner’s ability to exercise team work is enhanced as they recognize the value of other’s ideas in role play activities.

• Digital literacy: learners connect using technology by using the internet to watch videos depicting different times of the day and

other social media sites and applications.

Values:
Respect: is promoted as the learner appreciates diverse facial expressions of their peers during conversations from others during conversations.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Self -esteem is enhanced as learners confidently take turns in conversations using facial expressions appropriately for effective

communication.

Link to other learning areas:

Mathematic Activities: as learners relate the concept of time when identifying activities done at different times of the day.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Video clips and/or pictures, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners, adapted

digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand

Other Related Service Providers: Resource person, speech therapist, Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist.
